title: Virtual receptionist cost for restaurants
description: Compare virtual receptionist cost for a restaurant, including monthly fees and per-order pricing, so you can weigh the options.
question: What is the virtual receptionist cost for a restaurant, and how do I compare it with phone staff or delivery apps?
answer: For a restaurant, virtual receptionist cost usually falls into two buckets: fixed monthly fees or per-order pricing. ROAL uses per completed phone order at $0.90, with no monthly fee, setup fee, per-minute fee, or contract, and free calls, questions, and test calls. intro:
A restaurant virtual receptionist often costs either a fixed monthly fee or a per-order fee. With ROAL, the cost is **$0.90 per completed phone order** only, with no monthly fee, setup fee, per-minute fee, or contract.

For a busy takeout shop, that difference matters. If your phone is ringing for hours, the real question is not “what is the cheapest plan?” but “what do I pay when calls actually turn into paid tickets?”

sections.h2: What does virtual receptionist cost usually include?
sections.body:
For restaurant owners, the phrase **virtual receptionist cost** can hide a few different billing styles. Some tools charge a monthly subscription just to be on, whether the phone rings or not. Human answering services usually bill per minute or per call. Some restaurant phone tools charge per location, which can be fine for a small shop but adds up fast if you run more than one place.

Here is a simple way to break it down before you buy anything:

| Cost type | What you pay for | What to ask |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly fee | Paying to keep the service active | Is it charged even in slow months? |
| Per-minute fee | Time spent on each call | Does a longer menu question cost more? |
| Per-call fee | Each answered call | What counts as answered? |
| Per-order fee | Completed orders only | Does it charge when the order reaches the kitchen? |

A practical example: say you get 300 calls a month, but only 80 become real orders. A monthly plan charges you for the full month either way. A per-order model charges only for the 80 orders that actually land on the kitchen screen.

sections.h2: How much should a restaurant expect to pay each month?
sections.body:
Many AI phone tools for restaurants charge a fixed monthly fee per location, often around **$79 to $599**. That can be a fair fit if you want a predictable bill, but it means you pay even in a slow week. Human answering services often bill by minute or by call, which can be hard to predict if your calls run long or callers ask about specials, hours, parking, or delivery zones.

ROAL’s pricing is different: **$0.90 per completed phone order**. That means a confirmed order whose ticket reaches the kitchen screen. No monthly fee, no setup fee, no per-minute fee, and no contract. Calls, questions, and test calls are unlimited and free.

A simple monthly math example:
- Say you complete 200 phone orders in a month.
- At $0.90 each, that would be **$180**.
- Plug in your own number of completed orders to see your cost.

If you want to compare this against a fixed monthly plan, use your own expected order count. A slow month and a rush month should not cost the same if the tool is only there to capture real phone orders.

sections.h2: How do I compare it with phone staff or delivery apps?
sections.body:
The easiest comparison is to look at the cost of one captured order, not just the sticker price. A receptionist, host, or dedicated phone worker costs wages, breaks, training time, and coverage for slow periods. Delivery apps commonly charge restaurants roughly **15% to 30% commission per order**, which is a very different cost structure from a phone host.

Use this simple swap-in example:

1. Pick your average phone order, say **$28**.
2. Pick your monthly phone order count, say **150**.
3. Compare three cost styles:

| Option | Example cost math | What to notice |
|---|---|---|
| ROAL | 150 orders × $0.90 = $135 | Costs only on completed orders |
| Monthly tool | Flat fee, say $199 | Same bill even if orders are light |
| Delivery app commission | $28 × 20% = $5.60 per order; 150 orders = $840 | Usually much higher per order |

The point is not that one model is always best. The point is that restaurant owners should compare costs using their own order volume, not only the monthly sticker price. If your phone orders are frequent, per-order pricing can be easier to tie directly to revenue.

sections.h2: What setup work should I expect before I pay anything?
sections.body:
A good restaurant phone host should be quick to test. With ROAL, the owner pastes the restaurant website, Google Maps link, or just the name and city at /try. ROAL reads the menu, prices, hours, and address from public pages and builds a phone host in about two minutes. The owner can test-call it in the browser, and there is no sign-up needed for that test.

That matters when you are comparing virtual receptionist cost, because setup time is part of the real cost too. If you need a long onboarding call, manual menu entry, or a week of back-and-forth before you can even hear the phone host, you are paying with time.

A quick owner checklist:
- Paste your website or Google Maps link.
- Test the phone host right away.
- Confirm the menu, hours, address, and parking details.
- Upload a menu if your public pages are messy or incomplete.
- Decide whether to forward all calls, only busy calls, or unanswered calls.

ROAL also gives each location its own phone line automatically once the owner claims the host. The restaurant keeps its own number, and forwarding can be turned off any time.

sections.h2: How does the cost connect to real phone orders in the kitchen?
sections.body:
The best pricing model is the one that matches kitchen work. If a caller places a pickup order, the host takes items, sizes, modifiers, and notes, collects the caller’s name and phone, quotes a ready time, and confirms the order back. Then a clean ticket goes to the kitchen screen. That is a completed order, and that is what ROAL charges for.

Here is a worked example you can copy:
- Say your average phone order is **$22**.
- Say you get **120 completed phone orders** in a month.
- ROAL cost: **120 × $0.90 = $108**.
- If your average order grows to **$35**, your ROAL fee stays the same per completed order.

That structure is helpful for pizza shops, delis, and takeout spots because the phone can handle both short orders and detailed ones. ROAL can also speak the caller’s language, take reservation requests, and hand allergy-sensitive questions, catering, complaints, or manager requests to staff with a summary. It does not take card numbers over the phone, so payment still happens at pickup or however your restaurant already takes it.

sections.h2: How can I reduce the cost without losing calls?
sections.body:
You do not have to treat every call the same. The cheapest setup is the one that sends routine calls to the phone host and keeps unusual calls with staff. With ROAL, forwarding can be set so the host answers all calls, or only when busy or unanswered. That gives you a way to protect the front counter during rushes without paying for extra staff time on every ring.

A practical call-routing checklist:
- Route busy and missed calls to the host first.
- Keep complaints and manager requests for staff.
- Let the host answer hours, menu, parking, and address questions.
- Use the inbox for questions the host could not answer once, so it learns them from then on.

If you want to see whether this pencils out, compare your current phone costs against the tool’s cost per completed order. A useful next step is to review [Pricing](/pricing) and then plug your own order count into the numbers. If you want a simple comparison across pricing models, [this per-order vs monthly breakdown](/blog/per-minute-vs-per-order-pricing) is a good companion read.

For owners who want a quick starting point, you can [build a free test host](/try) from your website and hear how it handles your menu before you change your forwarding.

faq.q: What is a normal virtual receptionist cost for a restaurant?
faq.a: Many restaurant AI phone tools charge a flat monthly fee, often roughly $79 to $599 per location. Human answering services usually bill per minute or per call. A per-order model like ROAL is different because you pay only when a completed phone order reaches the kitchen screen.

faq.q: Is per-order pricing cheaper than a monthly fee?
faq.a: It depends on your call volume and how many calls become orders. If you have a slow month, per-order pricing can cost less because you are not paying a flat fee just to stay active. If you have a very high order count, you should plug in your numbers and compare both models before deciding.

faq.q: Does ROAL charge for test calls or questions?
faq.a: No. Calls, questions, and test calls are unlimited and free. ROAL only charges $0.90 per completed phone order, meaning a confirmed order whose ticket reached the kitchen screen.

faq.q: Do I still need staff to handle every call?
faq.a: No. ROAL can handle hours, address, parking, menu questions, pickup and delivery orders, and reservation requests. But tricky calls still go to staff, including catering, complaints, allergy-sensitive questions, and manager requests, with a summary so your team can pick it up fast.
